approach: The montage is fixed, so the 1.5 minutes has to come out of about 3.7 minutes of dialogue. Most of it is in two places: SJ's half-apology about the degree at the top, and a second lap of the review argument (guided tour, marking its own homework, evals) that repeats points s01 and s01b already made. The rest is clause trims inside SJ's longer speeches. Brendan keeps at least two attempts to show his process, and SJ talks over every one.

suggestions.title: Cut SJ's half-apology about the degree
suggestions.why: The degree insult has already played out: s01 has it on stage and s01b has Kristina weighing an HR conversation. SJ's later apology in s19_l8 ("I know I gave you some shit for it") lands harder if he hasn't already half-apologised in the first act. If you also take the trim to s01c_l6, the narrator line goes straight into SJ's reason for calling.
suggestions.keeps: The insult as a character engine (s01, s01b). SJ's "I'm the one following the rules" defence comes back in full in s11b_l5. The scene still opens on SJ calling about the PR.

against.s01c_l2: Before you say anything. The Kristina thing this morning, what I said about her degree. That landed like shit. I know. I shouldn't have said it like that.
against.s01c_l4: But I wasn't wrong to be worried! I'm not trying to bully her, I'm just tired of getting overridden when I'm the one following the rules! I just... struggle to convey that, I guess.
against.s01c_l5: …Honestly? If you said it to her the way you just said it to me, it'd go a lot better.

suggestions.riskWhy: Loses SJ's only act-one acknowledgement that the degree comment went too far, plus Brendan coaching him, but no plot fact: the insult itself plays in s01 and s01b, and 'following the rules' returns in s11b_l5. Note the separate conflict with #91, which cuts the later apology in s19_l8.
loses: Character: SJ admitting the degree comment 'landed like shit' and failing to say it to Kristina (only later echo is s19_l8, which #91 would cut)
Character: Brendan quietly coaching SJ ('If you said it to her the way you just said it to me')
Character: SJ's 'I'm the one following the rules' self-image, first stated here (carried in s11b_l5)
suggestions.dismissedBy: claude 2026-10-09: cuts comedy or removes narration

suggestions.title: Cut the second lap: guided tour, homework, evals
suggestions.why: "Marking its own homework" is SJ's s01 line, and s01b_l38 repeats it before Brendan answers it in s01b_l44 to l46 (he writes the integration tests himself). Here it is said a third time and answered a second time. With these lines gone, s01c_l15 ("blindly believing in autocomplete") leads straight into s01c_l19 ("You've all decided the thing is smart"), and that still makes sense.
suggestions.keeps: Guardrail 1: Brendan still tries to show SJ his process in s01c_l9, l12 and l14, and SJ cuts across him each time. The stage direction at s01c_l20, where he gives up, still plays.

against.s01c_l16: SJ, please, give me two minutes. Let me actually show you how I reviewed it. There's the plan, there's the whole session, the tests I wrote, the way I...
against.s01c_l17: I don't need the guided tour of Cursor, Brendan. I know how it works better than you do. Like I said three hours ago, the AI wrote the code and wrote the tests that say the code's fine. It's marking its own homework.
against.s01c_l18: …I wrote the evals myself actually, against our staging env...

suggestions.riskWhy: Touches guardrail 1: it removes two of Brendan's five attempts to show SJ his process, including the only one where he names concrete evidence (evals he wrote against staging), leaving his try-and-get-cut-off pattern noticeably thinner. Separately, it conflicts with #19 in s01b, which cuts the s01b_l44 to l46 answer this relies on.
loses: Character: Brendan pleading for 'two minutes' to show the plan, session and tests (guardrail 1)
Character: SJ's tech vanity, 'I know how it works better than you do'
Plot: Brendan wrote the evals himself against staging (answered differently in s01b_l46, nowhere else in this form)
Colour: SJ's 'like I said three hours ago' tying the call back to the standup

suggestions.why: This is an alternative to the second-lap cut, not an addition to it. suggestions.keeps: If this is taken alone, Brendan's attempts in s01c_l9, l12, l16 and l18 survive. Do not take it together with the second-lap cut: Brendan would be left with only l9 and l12, which is the guardrail's minimum, and the dialogue would jump from "What does it do?" to s01c_l19.

Also loses SJ's read-it-line-by-line rule, which is the position Brendan is trying to answer.

Character: SJ's 'hold the whole thing in your head, that's the job' creed (his autocomplete view returns in s11b_l64)

ifDeleted.summary: s01c is the main home of guardrail 1: Brendan earnestly tries to walk SJ through his plan, session and evals, and SJ talks straight over him. It also gives SJ his half-apology for the degree remark, his 'marking its own homework' and 'fast intern' arguments, and the image of SJ alone hunting the diff for a flaw he cannot find. Deleting it leaves s01b_l51's promised one-on-one unpaid and leaves s11b and s07_l21 echoing a failure the audience never saw.

lost.what: Brendan earnestly tries to show SJ his agentic process (plan, session, his own evals) and it goes over SJ's head
Pays off s01b_l50-l51: Kristina asks if Brendan has shown SJ, Brendan says he needs one on one time where SJ lets him show him
SJ half-apologises for the degree remark, then justifies it ('I'm tired of getting overridden'); Brendan's note that saying it that way would land better
SJ's 'marking its own homework' line, which Kristina quotes in s01b_l38; SJ says it nowhere else in the play
SJ's core anti-AI argument: read every line, hold it in your head, the AI is a confident intern who never says 'I don't know'
